key_insight: Low voltage-prediction errors do not necessarily imply physically feasible or operationally reliable neural power flow solutions under system shifts.
engineering_relevance: Physics-based checks can help engineers assess neural power flow solvers beyond accuracy before deployment under changing grid topologies and load distributions.
method: Evaluate topology shifts, load distribution shifts, mixed-topology training, and combined shifts.
Measure KCL gaps, branch-flow gaps, KVL residuals, and continuous feasibility scores.
Report strict, practical, and relaxed power flow feasibility rates alongside voltage-domain errors.
evidence_signal: Eight ANN architectures, including graph-input models, load-only baselines, and physics-informed neural networks, are evaluated under consistent settings across four case studies.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical feasibility results or threshold definitions, limiting assessment of deployment readiness.
paper_title: Beyond Accuracy: Physics-Informed Evaluation of ANN-based Power Flow Solvers under System Shift
